key_insight: The paper shows that adding a convex regularizer to stochastic nonsmooth nonconvex optimization does not increase oracle complexity when using an online-to-nonconvex conversion framework.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretically optimal recipe for training constrained or regularized models, including neural networks, with provable stationarity guarantees under stochastic gradients or function-value access.
method: Extend online-to-nonconvex conversion to composite objectives.
Use online mirror descent with losses that include the regularizer directly, not just its linearization.
Derive optimal Goldstein-stationarity rates for both first-order and zeroth-order oracles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical rates of O(δ^-1 ε^-3) stochastic gradient queries and O(d δ^-1 ε^-3) function-value queries, matching the best known noncomposite results, and mentions numerical experiments.
watch_item: The guarantees are for Goldstein-type stationarity and depend on stochastic oracle access, so practical performance may still vary with tuning, dimension, and the choice of regularizer.
paper_title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity
